items.title: Conseil des ministres du 29-07-2026 : Magal de Touba, réforme de l’école et présidence de la CEDEAO au menu
items.description: Réuni ce mercredi 29 juillet 2026 au Palais de la République sous la présidence de Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, le Conseil des ministres a été dominé par les préparatifs du Magal de Touba, la refonte du système éducatif et le nouveau statut diplomatique du Sénégal, désormais à la tête de la CEDEAO. Le Magal de Touba, priorité sécuritaire et logistique À quelques jours de la 132e édition du Magal, prévue le dimanche 2 août, le chef de l'État a demandé au gouvernement de prendre « toutes les dispositions logistiques et sécuritaires requises », avec une vigilance particulière sur « la sécurité et la circulation routières ». Le communiqué rappelle que cet événement religieux figure, depuis 2025, sur la liste nationale du patrimoine culturel à sauvegarder. Le Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye a par ailleurs indiqué avoir effectué un séjour à Touba les 26 et 27 juillet, au cours duquel il a rendu visite à Serigne Mountakha Bassirou Mbacké, khalife général des Mourides, pour « réitérer l'accompagnement et l'engagement de l'État » dans le développement de la ville, notamment sur l'hydraulique et l'assainissement. École : vers une « transformation consensuelle » Décrivant l'école comme « le socle de la République », le Président a félicité les lauréats des examens de l'année et demandé aux ministres de l'Éducation, de la Formation professionnelle et de l'Enseignement supérieur de procéder « sans délai » à l'évaluation globale de l'année scolaire 2025-2026, sous la supervision du Premier ministre. Il a également réclamé une accélération des chantiers de constructions scolaires et universitaires, se félicitant de la livraison des infrastructures de l'Université du Sine Saloum El Hadji Ibrahima Niass. Le chef de l'État présidera par ailleurs, le jeudi 30 juillet, la cérémonie de remise des prix aux lauréats du Concours général 2026. Recherche et intelligence artificielle Revenant sur la rentrée solennelle de l'Académie nationale des Sciences et Techniques, tenue le 21 juillet sur le thème de la souveraineté alimentaire, le président a demandé un renforcement des moyens de l'institution pour appuyer l'Agenda de Transformation Sénégal 2050. Il a instruit la mise en place d'un « Fonds national de promotion de la recherche et de l'innovation », ainsi qu'une réflexion sur un futur Conseil national de la Recherche et de l'Innovation, dans la foulée du déploiement annoncé d'un plan national dédié à l'intelligence artificielle. Justice et service public : plusieurs chantiers ouverts Le chef de l'État a par ailleurs annoncé avoir reçu le rapport 2025 du Médiateur de la République ainsi que les rapports 2024 et 2025 de l'Observateur national des lieux de privation de liberté. Il a demandé au gouvernement de « corriger les manquements signalés » et d'appliquer les recommandations formulées, tout en engageant une réflexion sur l'actualisation du cadre institutionnel du Médiateur. Au ministre de la Justice, il a fixé plusieurs urgences : le traitement définitif des affaires en appel, la révision du cadre réglementaire pour les personnes déficientes mentales, et la modernisation de l'administration pénitentiaire, avec la finalisation du statut des personnels et d'un futur Code pénitentiaire. JOJ Dakar 2026 : dernière ligne droite Alors que les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse entrent dans leur « dernière phase » de préparatifs, avec la réception des infrastructures sportives, le président a demandé au Premier ministre de finaliser rapidement les travaux routiers et d'aménagement liés à l'événement, en insistant sur la mobilisation des populations et des collectivités territoriales. Sénégal-CEDEAO : un « plébiscite sans précédent » Le communiqué consacre un développement appuyé au sommet de la CEDEAO tenu le 19 juillet à Freetown, que le président a qualifié de « succès diplomatique » marqué par un « plébiscite sans précédent » pour le Sénégal. Bassirou Diomaye Faye y a été désigné président en exercice de l'organisation pour un an, tandis que le général d'armée aérienne Birame Diop a été porté à la présidence de la Commission de la CEDEAO pour 2026-2030. Le sommet a en outre confié à Dakar le rôle de facilitateur dans le processus de sortie de crise en Guinée-Bissau. Le Président Faye a salué ces résultats comme le reflet du « rayonnement diplomatique du Sénégal » et remercié ses homologues ouest-africains, avant de mentionner sa visite de travail effectuée le 28 juillet au Mali, à l'invitation du général Assimi Goïta, président de la transition malienne. items.title: Boaduwaa strikes as Ghana beat WAFCON debutants Cape Verde
items.description: Cape Verde lost 2-0 to Ghana in Morocco on Wednesday as they failed to match the feat of fellow Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) debutants Malawi. Malawi, the lowest ranked of the 16 title contenders, stunned defending champions Nigeria 3-2 on Tuesday with the Chawinga sisters, Temwa and Tabitha, scoring the three goals. Cape Verde, 60 places below Ghana in the world rankings, were hoping to emulate Malawi by defeating Ghana, bronze medallists at the last WAFCON. The tiny nation also wanted to capture the imagination of the football world like the men’s national team at the recent World Cup, where they took Argentina to extra time before bowing out. Representing an archipelago off the west coast of Africa with a population of just over 500,000, Cape Verde fell behind after only seven minutes when Doris Boaduwaa scored. Cape Verde fell further behind on 54 minutes as Eleia Vieira conceded an own goal. A cross struck her and beat goalkeeper Jacinta Rodrigues. Rodrigues was constantly in action with her agility and bravery sparing the islanders a heavier loss at the Moulay Rachid Stadium in Moroccan commercial capital Casablanca. Ghana pressed forward from the kick-off of the opening Group D match and were rewarded when Boaduwaa latched on to a long, lofted pass from Portia Boakye and lobbed the ball over Rodriques. Boaduwaa, a 23-year-old striker from the Hapoel Jerusalem club, could have had a hat-trick before half-time thanks to her prowess on the ground and in the air. Cape Verde came closest to scoring after falling two goals behind when an audacious shot from the centre circle by Ivania Moreira forced a save from alert Cynthia Konlan. The losers were reduced to 10 players two minutes into added time when Kleydiana Borges was shown a straight red card after a VAR review for fouling Linda Ansah. items.title: Argentina players face FIFA investigation over World Cup final altercation with Spain
items.description: FIFA announced Wednesday that it had opened proceedings into some Argentina players for their behaviour after losing the World Cup to Spain. A handful of Argentina players and staff confronted their Spanish rivals after the final whistle of the final in New York which Spain won 1–0 after extra time. Argentina players including Nahuel Molina, Thiago Almada and Leandro Paredes, as well as Argentinian official Roberto Ayala, were involved in the incidents, as was Spain’s Pablo Martin Paez Gavira. Disciplinary proceedings were opened with the quintet facing charges from assault to unsporting behaviour. FIFA will also investigate an incident following Argentina’s 2-1 semi-final victory over England in which players held up a banner that read: “Las Malvinas son Argentinas” (The Falklands are Argentine). FIFA said the proceedings would target potential breaches of the world governing body’s articles on using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, discrimination and racist abuse, and order and security at matches. The latter comes “in light of discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators in relation to several matches of the representative team of Argentina at the FIFA World Cup 2026”. Vanguard News The post Argentina players face FIFA investigation over World Cup final altercation with Spain appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Government rolls out six new regulations to operationalise EPA Act 1124
items.description: The government has announced the passage of six new regulations to facilitate the effective implementation of the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) Act, 2025 (Act 1124), as part of efforts to strengthen environmental governance and enforcement across the country. The new regulations cover Environmental Assessment, Effluent Management, Air Quality, Ozone Protection, Petroleum Operations, and the Certification of Air Conditioners. Existing environmental regulations, guidelines and operational manuals have also been revised to ensure they are fully aligned with the new legislation. The Acting Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, Emmanuel Armah Kofi Buah, disclosed this on the floor of Parliament while responding to a question on the operationalisation of the new EPA Act and the institutional reforms being introduced to strengthen enforcement. He said the EPA has already begun training its staff and other relevant stakeholders on the new legal requirements, operational procedures and enforcement tools to ensure the effective implementation of the law. Mr Buah further indicated that the recruitment of additional personnel and the establishment of new EPA offices in districts across the country would significantly enhance the Authority’s operational capacity to address emerging environmental challenges. He expressed confidence that the institutional reforms and supporting regulations would strengthen compliance with environmental laws and improve the EPA’s ability to protect Ghana’s environment.

items.title: Services bancaires : la Banque d’Algérie fixe six exigences aux banques
items.description: Après les exportations hors hydrocarbures, la Banque d’Algérie a fixé ce mercredi six exigences aux banques. Objectif : faciliter l’accès des ménages aux produits et services bancaires. « Afin de renforcer l’accès des ménages aux produits et services bancaires et de contribuer au développement de l’inclusion financière, les banques et les établissements financiers sont tenus de prendre toutes les dispositions nécessaires pour assurer une prise en charge diligente et adaptée des besoins de leur clientèle », a demandé la Banque d’Algérie dans sa note n°3 adressée aux banques ce mercredi 29 juillet. Le régulateur a fixé un délai de deux mois pour l’exécution de cette feuille de route. En tout, il a arrêté six objectifs à atteindre. Ce que la Banque d’Algérie exige des banques Il s’agit de simplifier les procédures d’accès à l’ensemble des produits et services bancaires et de réduire les délais de traitement des demandes, d’assurer une prise en charge diligente des demandes, notamment en matière d’ouverture de comptes bancaires, de services de paiement et services monétiques, d’accès au financement, de produits d’épargne, y compris ceux relevant de la finance islamique, de développer une offre diversifiée de produits et services bancaires adaptée aux besoins des ménages. La Banque d’Algérie exige des banques de renforcer la couverture géographique de l’offre de produits et services bancaires par le développement du réseau d’agences ainsi que des canaux numériques, dans une logique de complémentarité. Le régulateur demande aux banques aussi d’assurer l’accessibilité des produits et services bancaires aux personnes à mobilité réduite, aux personnes âgées ainsi qu’aux autres catégories de clientèle nécessitant des modalités de prise en charge adaptées et de renforcer l’information, le conseil et l’accompagnement de la clientèle en vue d’améliorer sa connaissance des produits et services bancaires et d’en favoriser une utilisation accrue. Les banques ont un délai de deux mois pour réaliser les objectifs fixés par la Banque d’Algérie La Banque d’Algérie a ajouté que les banques et les établissements financiers sont « tenus de prendre toutes les dispositions organisationnelles et opérationnelles nécessaires, au plus tard le 30 septembre 2026, pour assurer la mise en œuvre effective de la présente note au niveau de l’ensemble de leur réseau, d’en assurer le suivi régulier et de déployer les actions appropriées en vue d’atteindre les objectifs fixés ». Mardi, la Banque d’Algérie a adressé une note à l'ensemble des banques intermédiaires agréées pour les informer que « toute opération d'exportation de biens et de services doit obligatoirement être domiciliée dans un délai maximal de 48 heures à compter de la réception du dossier complet ». L’article Services bancaires : la Banque d’Algérie fixe six exigences aux banques est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 2027: INEC records 10.18m new voters as CVR ends
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC has announced that a total of 3,867,997 Nigerians successfully completed the Continuous Voter Registration CVR exercise at the end of Phase III, Week Eleven, which concluded on Sunday, July 26, 2026. Checks revealed that millions of eligible voters may have been added to the voter register during the three phases of the exercise so far. During the first phase, about 2,572,054 voters completed their registration, while 3,748,704 voters were added at the end of the second phase, bringing the cumulative figure to about 10,188,755 when added to the Phase III total. There are currently over 93 million registered voters in Nigeria. INEC will still embark on a de-duplication process for the over 10 million fresh registrants in order to remove multiple registrants before adding the cleaned figure to the National Register of Voters. According to the commission’s infographic released on Wednesday night, 2,697,863 registrants completed the exercise through physical registration centres, while 1,170,134 registered online before completing the required process. This shows that physical registration remained the preferred option, accounting for nearly 70 per cent of all completed registrations. A breakdown by state indicates that Kano State recorded the highest number of completed registrations with 330,906, representing 8.55 per cent of the nationwide total. Lagos State followed with 181,254 registrations (4.69 per cent), while Delta State ranked third with 166,895 registrations (4.31 per cent). Edo State registered 156,150 voters, and Sokoto State recorded 145,160. Other states with high registration figures include Ebonyi (146,507), Taraba (141,649), Ogun (136,921), Bauchi (128,753), Jigawa (125,155), and Oyo (125,144). At the lower end of the chart, Ekiti State recorded 2,276 completed registrations, while Ondo State registered 23,824. Plateau State had 41,993 completed registrations, and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) recorded 56,285. The commission also noted that Osun State recorded no registrations during the period because the Continuous Voter Registration exercise was suspended ahead of the forthcoming governorship election, in line with Section 9(6) of the Electoral Act 2022. INEC said the figures reflect completed online and physical registrations across the country as the nationwide CVR exercise progresses toward expanding voter participation ahead of future elections. items.title: Fête du Trône : texte intégral du discours royal
items.description: Le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu L'assiste, a adressé, mercredi soir, un Discours à Son peuple fidèle à l’occasion du 27e anniversaire de l’accession du Souverain au Trône de Ses Glorieux Ancêtres. Voici le texte intégral du Discours Royal: « Louange à Dieu, Prière et salut sur le Prophète, Sa famille et Ses compagnons. Cher peuple, C’est avec une immense fierté et une profonde satisfaction que Nous célébrons aujourd’hui le vingt-septième anniversaire de Notre Accession au Trône. Voilà vingt-sept ans que fut accomplie la volonté du Seigneur de Me confier la charge de présider à tes destinées. La mission est noble et la tâche immense. En pleine résonance avec la Parole du Très-Haut : « Si vous êtes reconnaissants, je vous accorderai certainement plus de faveurs », Nous Lui rendons grâce du bienfait qu’Il nous dispense en Nous guidant sur le chemin de la réussite pour combler tes attentes et répondre à tes préoccupations. Jamais la poursuite d’une gloire personnelle, ni l’envie de consécration par le titre de « Leader continental ou international » n’ont été une fin pour Moi. En revanche, Mon unique souci a toujours été de M’acquitter au mieux de la responsabilité qui M’incombe de te servir, en veillant à ce que tous les Marocains puissent vivre dignement, en citoyens libres. Aujourd’hui, l’examen de ce que nous avons réalisé ensemble M’inspire honneur et fierté au regard de l’importance des acquis et Me rend pleinement optimiste au sujet de l’avenir. Plus qu’un mobile de satisfaction personnelle, ce bilan insuffle plutôt un sentiment gratifiant de confiance et de sérénité qui Nous donne de la force et Nous motive pour aller de l’avant et poursuivre notre entreprise. Le résultat de notre action ne tient pas du hasard : il est bel et bien la conséquence d’une vision stratégique claire et d’une doctrine de pouvoir dont les maîtres-mots sont la prise d’initiative, le suivi rigoureux, l’autocritique constructive et la réelle volonté d’aborder l’avenir avec détermination et positivité. Cher peuple, Notre pays se trouve aujourd’hui à une étape-charnière de son processus de développement, où un idéal de confiance et d’optimisme doit l’emporter sur toute rhétorique susceptible de nourrir désespoir et frustration. Ce qui rend le plus fier, c’est la sécurité et la stabilité qui règnent au Maroc, ainsi que le fonctionnement efficace des institutions publiques. De fait, dans un contexte régional et international en proie à de nombreuses convulsions et à des tensions multiples, la stabilité politique et institutionnelle constitue une denrée rare et un atout d’une valeur inestimable. Aujourd’hui, la stabilité est la variable-clé dans l’équation du développement au Maroc. Elle est aussi le capital stratégique qui fait la fierté du pays. Cher peuple, Pays à l’histoire millénaire, le Maroc puise sa force dans ses traditions ancestrales d’Etat-nation où les institutions remplissent leur rôle dans un esprit d’harmonie et de complémentarité. C’est pourquoi les réalisations se poursuivent avec l’efficacité requise, et que le pays réussit, par-delà les difficultés et les contraintes, à relever les défis. A cet égard, le Maroc a su donner la mesure de son efficacité à travers la bonne organisation de manifestations continentales et internationales. Une telle maîtrise lui a valu des marques d’admiration et d’estime de par le monde, sans toutefois manquer de faire des envieux en certaines occasions. En outre, le Maroc a fait montre d’une grande résilience face aux catastrophes et aux crises, comme cela a été notamment le cas lors de la gestion proactive des inondations qui ont touché le Gharb et le nord du pays. A la faveur de la sécurité et de la stabilité ambiantes, associées à l’efficacité institutionnelle, les indicateurs positifs se multiplient dans tous les secteurs d’activité, confortant ainsi la dynamique d’émergence économique et sanctuarisant davantage la souveraineté nationale. De fait, le taux de croissance s’est situé autour de 4,9% au titre de 2025, et il est attendu de réaliser un taux équivalent ou supérieur en 2026. S’agissant d’agriculture, le Maroc a connu une importante pluviométrie et une bonne campagne agricole. De cette conjoncture favorable, le pays sort avec une sécurité hydrique et alimentaire plus renforcée. Par ailleurs, comme en témoigne notamment l’évolution positive des indicateurs industriels, le Maroc a su consolider son statut de pôle attractif pour les investissements à vocation industrielle, touristique et financière. De fait, les secteurs de l’automobile, de l’aéronautique, des énergies renouvelables et des industries agroalimentaires forment aujourd’hui des piliers essentiels du tissu productif national, tant pour leur aptitude à drainer des investissements qu’en raison de leur capacité à créer de la richesse et des emplois. Aujourd’hui, le Maroc est devenu le premier exportateur automobile en Afrique, avec une capacité de production annuelle d’environ un million de véhicules. Aussi les secteurs de l’automobile et de l’aéronautique ont-ils vu leur part se porter à plus de 40% du total des exportations du Maroc, devançant par là même la filière des phosphates. En appui à cette tendance, Nous avons présidé en début d’année la cérémonie de lancement de nouvelles unités industrielles. Ainsi avons-Nous ouvert la voie pour que le Maroc fasse son entrée dans le cercle restreint des pays dotés des plus grands hubs spécialisés dans la fabrication des moteurs et des systèmes d’atterrissage des avions. Par le développement d’un secteur intégré de batteries électriques, le Maroc atteste également sa capacité à anticiper les transformations technologiques à venir, à s’intégrer dans les chaînes de production liées aux industries stratégiques. Portés par le même souffle d’innovation et de développement, des projets d’envergure sont en cours de réalisation afin que les énergies renouvelables deviennent un pilier de la sécurité énergétique et un levier d’attractivité pour les industries en quête d’une énergie compétitive et décarbonée. En appui à cette stratégie ambitieuse, la déclinaison opérationnelle de « l’Offre Maroc hydrogène vert » s’est amorcée par l’attribution d’autorisations à un premier groupe de mégaprojets. Cher peuple, Dans un contexte international marqué par le retour du protectionnisme et par l’impératif de sécurisation des chaînes d’approvisionnement et de production, Nous avons érigé le renforcement de la souveraineté nationale et l’autosuffisance stratégique en axes majeurs du développement industriel. Cette orientation trouve son illustration la plus éloquente dans les industries agroalimentaires et pharmaceutiques qui couvrent désormais près de 80% des besoins nationaux. D’un autre côté, l’installation d’une base industrielle et technologique de défense et de cybersécurité concourra, graduellement, à consolider la souveraineté en matière de défense et à générer des opportunités de développement, confortant ainsi le statut de puissance régionale qui échoit à notre pays dans ces filières. Par ailleurs, le secteur touristique a réalisé, au cours de l’année 2025, une performance historique en accueillant près de 20 millions de visiteurs, incluant les membres de la communauté marocaine résidant à l’étranger. Parallèlement à la promotion du secteur économique, Nous poursuivons le déploiement de multiples initiatives et de programmes de développement humain, notamment à travers la généralisation de la protection sociale. Notre but ultime est d’améliorer les conditions de vie des Marocains et d’instaurer la justice sociale et spatiale. À cet égard, Nous insistons sur la nécessité d’une mise en œuvre efficiente des programmes de développement territorial intégré, tout en Nous assurant qu’ils englobent toutes les régions, sans exception aucune. De surcroît, la dynamique de transformation économique et sociale exige la mobilisation de ressources financières d’une envergure inédite, dont l’essentiel doit provenir de financements domestiques. C’est pourquoi Nous exhortons le secteur financier national à continuer à accompagner l’investissement et les grands projets et à élargir qualitativement l’accès aux financements, bancaires et non bancaires, destinés aux petites et moyennes entreprises, à l'innovation, à l’industrialisation et à l'exportation. En outre, Nous aspirons à ce que le secteur financier se montre plus ouvert et plus novateur pour assurer une mobilisation optimale de l’épargne nationale, notamment institutionnelle, et redynamiser les marchés financiers. Un coup d’accélérateur sera ainsi donné à la dynamique de développement du Maroc émergent. Cher peuple, Nous sommes parvenu, avec l’aide du Seigneur, à consolider la position du Maroc en tant qu’acteur international crédible, respecté et écouté. En effet, le Royaume s’affirme aujourd’hui comme un opérateur économique de premier plan et un associé sollicité pour être partie prenante à des partenariats nouveaux, équilibrés et tournés vers l’avenir. Fort de ces statuts, il est désormais en mesure d’interpeller l’ensemble de ses partenaires en toute confiance et transparence et de formuler, s’agissant des différentes questions bilatérales et des grandes problématiques internationales, des offres de partenariat constructives et des initiatives de coopération prometteuses. Agissant avec engagement et responsabilité, notre pays a fait également le choix de diversifier ses partenariats afin de renforcer ses capacités et d’en accroître la portée dans tous les domaines. Cher peuple, Ces acquis économiques et sociaux engrangés transcendent les mandats gouvernemental et parlementaire. Ils sont, en effet, le fruit d’une dynamique cumulative vertueuse, étalée sur des années de suite et favorisée par les orientations stratégiques de notre pays et la pertinence de ses choix majeurs. Nous formons le vœu qu’au lendemain des prochaines législatives et de l’émergence consécutive d’un nouveau gouvernement, s’amorce un nouveau cycle dans notre trajectoire de développement, dont les maîtres-mots seront la préservation des acquis et la poursuite des projets et des réformes d'envergure. Cher peuple, La célébration de la Glorieuse Fête du Trône est l’occasion pour Nous d’exprimer à nouveau Notre fierté et l’estime que Nous portons à Nos Forces Armées Royales, à la Gendarmerie Royale, à l’Administration territoriale, à la Sûreté nationale, aux Forces Auxiliaires et à la Protection civile, toutes composantes confondues, pour leur dévouement et leur mobilisation constante, sous Notre commandement, à défendre l’unité nationale et à préserver la sécurité et la stabilité du pays. A cet égard, Nous nous remémorons avec une profonde déférence le souvenir des valeureux martyrs de la Nation, au premier rang desquels Notre Auguste Grand-Père, feu Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed V et Notre Illustre Père, feu Sa Majesté le Roi Hassan II, que Dieu les ait en Sa sainte miséricorde. Citons enfin, en guise de conclusion, le Verset qui décrète : « Dieu ne lèse pas les gens bienfaisants ». Wassalamou alaikoum wa rahmatoullah wa barakatouh ». items.title: The Anti-Democrat
items.description: Photographs by Nic Antaya Y ou won’t find a much harsher critic of the Democratic Party than the progressive trying to secure its nomination for Senate in Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed. When I caught up with him last week in Ann Arbor, he was at a café holding an outdoor roundtable with young voters, many of them college students or recent graduates. The normally voluble El-Sayed, drinking matcha and dressed casually in his signature tight black T-shirt and jeans, listened as much as he talked, and he heard the students describe their disillusionment with politics—and especially with Democratic candidates. “Your generation has a great bullshit meter, because you’re fed bullshit online all day,” El-Sayed told the group. “And the Democratic Party brand right now is so bullshit.” It was not a statement with which any of the students seemed to disagree. “You tell it like it is, and that’s what we young people want,” Joe Garris, the president of the College Democrats at Eastern Michigan University, told El-Sayed. “We don’t want to hear corporate answers anymore. We just want the straight truth.” One of the few factors that could impede a Democratic wave in this year’s midterms is the party’s own unpopularity; polling suggests that plenty of voters outside college campuses might also nod along to El-Sayed’s denunciation of Democrats. Antipathy toward the party is fueling the rise of populist insurgents such as El-Sayed, who castigate Democratic leaders like Chuck Schumer with nearly as much fervor as they criticize President Trump. Nowhere are the lines dividing Democrats more clearly drawn than in Michigan, a state that the party must win to have any real chance of retaking the Senate majority in November. Democrats have to flip four Republican-held seats without losing any of their own, and Michigan is the Democratic-held seat at the most risk of going red. (The incumbent, Senator Gary Peters, is retiring.) El-Sayed is battling Representative Haley Stevens in the August 4 primary, and the winner will face former Representative Mike Rogers, a formidable GOP candidate who came within roughly 20,000 votes of capturing Michigan’s other Senate seat two years ago. A 41-year-old doctor, Rhodes Scholar, and former county health director, El-Sayed is running as an unabashed critic of Israel and of corruption in both parties. He begins rallies with a call-and-response incantation of his campaign slogan: “Money out of … politics ! Money in your … pocket ! Medicare for … all !” I sat down with him after his event in Ann Arbor and asked him to specify the parts of the Democratic brand that he believes are “bullshit.” He began with some of his campaign themes and described Democrats as hypocrites in thrall to corporate donors. “You say you’re for human rights and can’t name a genocide a genocide,” El-Sayed said. “You say you want to give people health care but take money from the people who are keeping us from having health care. You say you want to stand up to Big Tech and take money from Big Tech.” Nic Antaya for The Atlantic A yard sign for Abdul El-Sayed in Ferndale, Michigan Nic Antaya for The Atlantic A person claps during an El-Sayed rally. “What are we actually for?” El-Sayed continued. “Are we just the permanent opposition party where ‘We’re not them’?” Then, referring to Republicans, he added, “At least they’re honest about who they are, for the most part.” This message should be familiar to those who have watched progressives and democratic socialists topple establishment favorites in New York City, Colorado, and Maine over the past several months. But Michigan is a state that Trump carried in 2024, and many Democrats fear that nominating a candidate who calls for abolishing ICE and establishing a single-payer health-care system is too big a risk in such a crucial year for the party. El-Sayed is also seeking to be the first Muslim senator at a time when some Republicans are fomenting unrestrained Islamophobia. A poll released on Tuesday found Stevens running even with Rogers while El-Sayed trailed him by 10 points in a hypothetical general-election matchup. [ Read: Something is happening in the Democratic base ] El-Sayed’s confidence can border on cockiness—some Democrats see his strident attacks on Stevens as demeaning or even sexist—and he has leaned into the electability debate. Ahead of the 2028 presidential race, he and his progressive supporters view the Michigan contest as an opportunity to extinguish what they see as stale Democratic beliefs about the types of candidates that can win in swing states. “This is just a different time, and this time calls for different kinds of candidates,” El-Sayed told me. “I hope that coming out of this election, the question of electability is no longer asked and interpreted in the same way.” He turns the argument back against Stevens, who has trailed in many polls despite benefiting from more than $60 million worth of ads bolstering her candidacy and attacking El-Sayed (about half of it coming from AIPAC). “If you can’t get elected without $60 million being spent for you, you can’t get elected. I’m so sorry,” El-Sayed said. The progressives’ chief data point is Trump’s 2024 win, which they interpret not as an endorsement of the president’s vision but as a rejection of Democrats and the political system more broadly. “You know what people hate more than Trump? Politics as usual. They hate politics as usual so much that they were willing to take Trump, warts and all,” El-Sayed told me. “So what happens if you offer them something that’s not politics as usual and isn’t a megalomaniacal billionaire narcissist? Well, let’s see.” Nic Antaya for The Atlantic Representative Haley Stevens laughs with supporters at the the Michigan Conference of Teamsters in Detroit on July 24. S tevens is in many ways the quintessential swing-state Democratic Senate candidate. A former Obama-administration official who worked on the auto-rescue task force during his first term, she won a Republican-held House seat in the Detroit suburbs in 2018. Her trajectory is broadly similar to that of Elissa Slotkin, a former CIA analyst and Pentagon official who was elected to Congress in 2018 and then narrowly defeated Rogers in the 2024 Senate race. In the House, Stevens has distinguished herself mostly through her loyalty to the Democratic leadership. She provided a reliable vote for President Biden’s major initiatives and enthusiastically backed his 2024 reelection bid even after many in the party were calling for him to drop out. Stevens’s campaign for Senate is well funded but also exceedingly conventional. She emphasizes her Michigan roots, her ties to Obama, and what she’s done for the state in Congress. Taking aim at El-Sayed’s personal wealth, Stevens likes to point out that she’s the only Senate candidate who’s not a millionaire, and she criticized him repeatedly for not releasing a complete financial disclosure. (He released it just before their final debate this week; it showed he’s worth as much as $2.1 million and earned income from a rental property his wife owns in Dubai.) Still, Stevens has not been able to generate the same amount of energy as El-Sayed, nor does she seem desperate to try. Over my three days in Michigan, he held at least eight events across the southern part of the state; she publicized just two, and her campaign declined to make her available for an interview. (It has helped El-Sayed that, unlike Stevens, he does not have to juggle campaigning with an important day job: “I’m Abdul. I’m 41, I’m unemployed, and I spend my time asking people for money,” El-Sayed joked to the students in Ann Arbor as he introduced himself.) [ Read: The return of the Democratic manly man ] Polling in the race has been murky. Surveys conducted by groups aligned with El-Sayed’s campaign have shown him up by double digits, as did an independent poll released today. But a Detroit News poll earlier this month found Stevens leading by nearly seven points. Supporters of Stevens had hoped the early-July exit of a third major candidate, State Senator Mallory McMorrow, would help her consolidate support. But one of McMorrow’s most prominent backers, Senator Elizabeth Warren, campaigned with El-Sayed over the weekend. With El-Sayed holding strong, Michigan’s most prominent Democrats have rallied behind Stevens in a bid to deny him the nomination. This spring, former Senator Debbie Stabenow endorsed Stevens. Then, soon after McMorrow dropped out, Stevens gained the endorsement of the retiring Peters, a former chair of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee who had earlier indicated he would stay out of the primary to succeed him. By far the biggest get for Stevens, however, was Governor Gretchen Whitmer , the state’s most popular Democrat, who announced her endorsement last Friday, a day before the start of early voting. Whitmer appeared that afternoon alongside Stevens and another key establishment backer, Representative James Clyburn, at a union rally in Detroit, where Stevens is counting on a big turnout among the city’s Black community. Without mentioning El-Sayed’s name, Whitmer strongly suggested that Stevens would be the stronger general-election candidate. “Michiganders understand better than anyone that our vote has a consequence for every American,” Whitmer said. “We also know that winning Michigan is as tough as it gets. But as someone who won statewide twice, I know Haley is tougher than the environment we’ve got to win in.” Nic Antaya for The Atlantic From left, Representative Pramila Jayapal, Senator Elizabeth Warren, Abdul El-Sayed, and Senator Chris Van Hollen in Ferndale, Michigan The primary race has turned nasty in its closing weeks, a concern for Democrats hoping that the party can unify to defeat Rogers, who has coasted to the GOP nomination without significant opposition. Stevens’s supporters erupted after El-Sayed implied to Semafor that she could not “string together two coherent sentences.” Soon after, he urged his supporters to stop making fun of Stevens “for things that have nothing to do with her policies or politics.” The flap may have helped Stevens find her voice—literally in a certain sense. She has turned her thick Michigan accent into a calling card of authenticity. “Some of you have seen, there’s those cool kids on the internet. They’re doing the cool-kid chatter. Some of them might be the coastal elites making fun of how I talk,” she told the crowd in Detroit, which laughed loudly. “They’re thinking they’re better than us. And what they don’t know is I am your voice, and their jokes and their criticism only makes me fight harder.” [ Read: One morning of controlled chaos in Maine ] As I talked with voters in Detroit and its suburbs, it seemed apparent that after such a bitter primary, either candidate could struggle to assemble the coalition they would need to win in November. Younger voters filled El-Sayed’s events, and several of them told me they weren’t sure they would support Stevens if she were the nominee. The image painted by El-Sayed of Stevens as a politician beholden to big-money interests had taken hold. “She would depress the youth vote,” Scott Siegal, a 24-year-old student, told me at an El-Sayed rally in Ferndale. If Stevens wins the nomination, he said, “I’d probably just not vote.” Colin Takata, a 27-year-old who works for an audio company, said of Stevens: “It almost feels like she’s a corporation in a trench coat.” At the Stevens rally, some of her supporters said they found El-Sayed likeable and appealing, but they favored Stevens’s experience and had concerns about his ability to win. “I have nothing against the brother. He’s a nice guy,” Robert Royster, a funeral director in Detroit, told me. “But she has receipts.” Others, however, took offense at El-Sayed’s treatment of Stevens. “From what I’ve heard, I don’t think he likes women,” Tyrone, a former auto worker who declined to give his last name in discussing such a fraught primary, told me. Long-simmering tensions between the Arab and Black communities in Detroit could also hamper El-Sayed. One of the first attendees I spoke with at the Stevens rally told me he didn’t care for El-Sayed in part because he doesn’t like Arab people. He was not the only person at the event who expressed such prejudice . Tyrone Carter, a state representative from Detroit backing Stevens, acknowledged the Arab-Black tensions in the city. “They’re real, and they exist,” he told me at the rally. S ome of the nation’s most popular progressives have come to Michigan to campaign with El-Sayed, including Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (as well as Warren). But an endorsement he values as highly as any of those has come from a Democrat with a far lower national profile, at least for now: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland. El-Sayed told me he wants to see Van Hollen replace Schumer as the Democratic leader in the Senate; Van Hollen says he’s “kicking the tires” on a 2028 presidential run instead, though he has notably not told El-Sayed to stop promoting him for the Senate leadership. [ Read: New York’s warning for Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer ] Nic Antaya for The Atlantic Stevens signs line the wall at the Michigan Conference of Teamsters. As a chair of the Democratic campaign committee first in the House and then, more recently, in the Senate, Van Hollen was responsible for recruiting candidates in the party’s toughest races. Many of those picks looked and sounded a lot more like Stevens than El-Sayed. But Van Hollen has become one of the Senate’s staunchest critics of Israel, and he told me the Trump era has changed his view about electability. “I think people want somebody who’s going to rock the boat,” he said, pointing to the election of “a convicted felon” to the presidency. “I think Donald Trump’s election was a symptom of a deeper unrest among voters. That unrest is real.” When I asked him if he agreed with El-Sayed’s assessment that the Democratic Party’s brand is “bullshit,” Van Hollen did not repeat the word, but he didn’t dispute it, either. Were he to win in November, El-Sayed would be the most progressive candidate elected in a swing state in modern times, but he keeps some space between himself and the leftward bound of today’s Democrats. He is not a democratic socialist, and when the question comes up, his position hews closer to Elizabeth Warren than to Bernie Sanders. “I think that capitalism is, when it actually works, an efficient way to allocate resources,” El-Sayed told me. “It’s not working right now.” “I know that the establishment desperately wants to turn me into a DSA candidate,” he went on. “I’m just not, and it bothers them so much.” El-Sayed is right about that. Neither his Democratic critics nor the Republicans who seem to be awaiting his nomination with glee are apt to make that distinction for Michigan voters. And if he defeats Stevens next week, the general election will test just how far the progressive movement can advance in this political era. It’s an opportunity that El-Sayed and his supporters have been waiting years to grab.

items.title: Mouhoun/Culture et artisanat à Douroula : La forge, un héritage au service du développement local
items.description: BURKINA-MOUHOUN-DOUROULA-CULTURE-ARTISANAT-FORGE Mouhoun/Culture et artisanat à Douroula : La forge, un héritage au service du développement local Douroula, 29 juil. 2026 (AIB)-A Douroula, dans la province du Mouhoun, la forge continue d'occuper une place de choix dans la vie socioéconomique des communautés. Héritier d'un savoir-faire ancestral, le forgeron Kassoum Go met en avant l'importance de cette activité dans le développement local, la production agricole, la cohésion sociale et le contexte sécuritaire actuel. Issu de la famille Go, reconnue comme la première lignée de forgerons installée à Douroula, Kassoum Go est aujourd'hui l'une des principales références de la profession dans la commune. Né à Douroula, il a été initié au métier par Modou Go, frère aîné de son père à Tchériba. Bien qu'il n'ait pas fréquenté l'école, il affirme avoir trouvé dans la forge une activité lui permettant de subvenir aux besoins de sa famille grâce au savoir-faire légué par ses ancêtres. Il a dit que les familles Go, Dao et Konaté constituent les principales lignées de forgerons établies dans la commune. Pour Kassoum Go, les forgerons ont toujours occupé une place centrale dans l'organisation des sociétés africaines. Il rappelle que depuis les royaumes anciens, chaque communauté s'appuyait sur ses artisans forgerons pour accompagner son développement. « Un village ne peut véritablement prospérer sans forgeron à défaut d'en disposer, il existe toujours un forgeron dans une localité voisine », soutient-il. L'artisan souligne que les outils fabriqués dans les ateliers de forge, notamment les dabas, haches, faucilles, charrues et autres équipements agricoles, accompagnent les producteurs depuis le défrichage des terres jusqu'aux récoltes. Cette contribution participe, selon lui, à l'amélioration de la production agricole et au renforcement de la sécurité alimentaire. Dans le contexte de la lutte contre le terrorisme, Kassoum Go indique, que des outils d’auto défenses ont été confectionnés afin de permettre aux forces engagées sur le théâtre des opérations de mieux sécuriser la localité. Evoquant les techniques de fabrication, il explique que les artisans utilisent désormais du fer acheté sur le marché, contrairement aux anciennes générations qui extrayaient elles-mêmes le minerai à partir des roches, une méthode aujourd'hui abandonnée en raison de sa pénibilité et de sa lenteur. La commune de Douroula abrite un haut fourneau d'extraction du fer inscrit au patrimoine mondial de l'UNESCO, ce qui témoigne de l'ancienneté de la tradition métallurgique dans cette partie du Burkina Faso. Face aux défis liés à la modernisation du secteur, le forgeron plaide pour un accompagnement accru des pouvoirs publics à travers la dotation en équipements modernes. Une telle mesure, estime-t-il, permettrait d'améliorer la qualité des productions, d'accroître leur compétitivité sur des marchés plus vastes et de faciliter l'accès des artisans aux marchés publics. Au-delà de sa dimension économique, Kassoum Go considère la forge comme un facteur de cohésion sociale fondé sur les valeurs de solidarité, d'entraide et de vivre-ensemble. Il a enfin invité les Burkinabè, gouvernants comme gouvernés, à cultiver la paix, l'unité et la solidarité afin de contribuer au développement durable du Burkina Faso. Agence d’information du Burkina TFT/HB/OO

items.title: 2022 nurse recruitment to begin before end of 2026 – Health Minister
items.description: The Minister for Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, has assured Parliament that the government is implementing a phased recruitment plan for nurses, midwives and other health professionals to strengthen healthcare delivery across the country. The Minister said the ongoing recruitment exercise is currently focused on the 2021 batch of nurses and midwives, with successful applicants already reporting to their respective duty stations. He added that the exercise forms part of efforts to address staffing gaps and improve healthcare services, particularly in underserved communities. Mr Akandoh further disclosed that the 2022 batch of nurses and midwives will be recruited before the end of 2026, while recruitment of the 2023 batch will follow, subject to financial clearance from the Ministry of Finance. He also revealed that a total of 16,000 health professionals are being recruited this year to boost the country’s health workforce. Speaking on the floor of Parliament while responding to questions from Members of Parliament, the Health Minister reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to the progressive recruitment of qualified health professionals in line with available financial resources and the staffing needs of health facilities across the country.

items.title: Women’s empowerment alone does not guarantee economic justice – Sheila Minkah-Premo
items.description: The Managing Consultant at ALC Law Consult, Sheila Minkah-Premo, has argued that empowering women through increased opportunities is not enough to achieve economic justice, insisting that deeper structural reforms are needed to ensure women own and control wealth. Speaking at the 10th anniversary lecture of the Young African Women’s Congress Network on Wednesday, July 29, she said true economic justice requires transforming the legal, economic and social systems that determine who owns productive assets and who benefits from economic growth. “Empowerment is a word that we all hear every day about. It’s been widely explored within development scholarship. While the literature offers diverse perspectives, it’s perhaps most useful to understand empowerment as both a process and an outcome through which individuals acquire the ability to make meaningful choices and to exercise agency over decisions affecting their lives,” she said. Mrs. Minkah-Premo explained that economic empowerment goes beyond increasing women’s incomes. “Building on this understanding, economic empowerment refers not only to increasing women’s incomes, but to expanding their capacity to access productive resources, participate in markets, influence economic decision-making, and exercise control over the benefits derived from their labor. However, empowerment alone does not necessarily produce economic justice.” She stressed that economic justice demands more than expanding opportunities for women. “Economic justice, therefore, requires more than expanding opportunities. It requires transforming the legal, economic, and social systems that determine who owns productive assets, who exercises control over resources, and who benefits from economic growth.” Mrs. Minkah-Premo also distinguished between income and wealth, noting that the two are often confused despite their significant differences. “Income is what we earn. Wealth is what we own. Wealth comprises land, housing, businesses, savings, investments, pensions, shares, and other productive assets capable of generating long-term economic security and intergenerational prosperity.” Citing the work of economist Thomas Piketty, she said patterns of wealth ownership often expose inequalities that are more entrenched than differences in income. “As Thomas Piketty has demonstrated, patterns of wealth ownership frequently reveal deeper and more enduring inequalities than income alone. Ownership, in turn, is not merely a question of legal title. Ownership is the ability to control, use, derive benefits from, and transfer productive assets.” She warned that countries could successfully empower women without ensuring they build meaningful wealth. “So these distinctions are important because they expose a reality that is often overlooked. A country may succeed in producing empowered women while still failing to produce women who own wealth in meaningful and transformative ways.” Defining economic justice, Mrs. Minkah-Premo described it as “a set of moral principles for building fair economic institutions focusing on equal opportunity, fair wealth distribution, and equitable working conditions.” “Its ultimate goal is to provide every person with sufficient material foundation to live a dignified, productive, and creative life,” she added.

items.title: Roi Mohammed VI : la stabilité du Maroc constitue sa force et son capital stratégique
items.description: La stabilité politique et institutionnelle du Maroc, une denrée rare et un atout d’une valeur inestimable, dans un contexte régional et international marqué par de nombreuses convulsions et des tensions multiples, constitue le capital stratégique et la force du Royaume, a affirmé le Roi Mohammed VI. Dans un discours à la Nation, ce mercredi à l'occasion de la fête du trône, le Souverain a rappelé que l'histoire millénaire du Maroc constitue sa force et en fait un Etat-Nation qui fait la fierté de tous les Marocains, mais aussi une variable-clé dans l’équation du développement, une motivation pour aller de l'avant, relever les défis, et poursuivre le travail au service des intérêts du pays. Dans ce sens, le Roi a indiqué n'avoir jamais recherché une gloire personnelle ni une reconnaissance pour un rôle de premier plan à l'échelle continentale ou internationale, soulignant que sa priorité demeure de servir le peuple marocain et de permettre à tous les citoyens de vivre dans la dignité. « En portant un regard sur le chemin parcouru ensemble, je ressens à la fois de la fierté pour les acquis réalisés et de l'optimisme pour l'avenir. Il ne s'agit pas d'une satisfaction personnelle, mais d'un sentiment de confiance et de sérénité qui nous donne la force et la motivation de poursuivre nos efforts » , a-t-il dit. Et d'ajouter que les réalisations accomplies ne sont pas le fruit du hasard, mais « d'une vision stratégique claire, d'un travail rigoureux fondé sur la bonne gouvernance, un suivi permanent, une autocritique constructive et une volonté résolue de préparer l'avenir dans un esprit positif ». The post Roi Mohammed VI : la stabilité du Maroc constitue sa force et son capital stratégique appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.description: BURKINA-KOOSIN-SANTE Koosin/Education : Une maladie contraint un élève de Dakuy à abandonner l'école Doumbala, 28 juil. 2026 (AIB)-L'élève Paulin Traoré de l'école de Dakuy a abandonné l'école à la suite d'une maladie. Son cursus a pris un coup à son CM1 à cause d'un mal qu'il traine depuis sa naissance et qui le ronge d'année en année. Paulin Traoré était un élève de l’école de Dakuy, un village situé à 12 hm, côté Est de Doumbala. Initialement apparu sous la forme d'un petit bouton sur la lèvre supérieure, le mal a évolué progressivement au fil des années. Au 28 juillet 2026, la lèvre supérieure a atteint un volume tel qu'elle recouvre complètement la lèvre inférieure. « J'ai abandonné l'école parce que je ne supportais plus le regard des autres élèves. Mon bouton est devenu très gros et cela me met mal à l'aise. C'est la honte qui m'a poussé à arrêter les cours, même si ce n'était pas mon choix. Aujourd'hui encore, je regarde avec envie les enfants partir à l'école et il m'arrive souvent d'en pleurer », a-t-il confié. Son plus grand souhait est de reprendre les études si la maladie guérit ou s'améliore. Selon les témoignages de son maître d’école, Paulin est une étoile et il a toujours été parmi les trois premiers. « Cette déperdition me touche profondément. Son avenir est hypothéqué », a ajouté l’enseignant. Le père de l'élève, Benoît Traoré, a expliqué qu'après une première consultation au Centre médical avec antenne chirurgicale (CMA) de Nouna, son fils a été référé à l'hôpital de Dédougou, avant d'être orienté à son tour vers Bobo-Dioulasso. « Arrivés à Bobo-Dioulasso, nos moyens financiers se sont rapidement épuisés. Malgré les dettes contractées pour assurer la prise en charge de mon fils, nous avons été contraints d'interrompre les soins et de regagner Bankuy. Depuis notre retour, la tumeur ne cesse de grossir et je me sens aujourd'hui impuissant face à la situation », a déclaré M. Traoré. Selon la mère de l’élève, Brigitte Diarra, le bouton était minuscule et la famille n'avait jamais su qu'il allait prendre cette tournure. Elle implore Dieu et toute personne de bonne volonté de leur venir en aide. Agence d’information du Burkina AC/HB/OO

items.title: WAFCON 2026: Black Queens make winning start with victory over Cape Verde
items.description: Ghana opened their 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) campaign with a 2-0 victory over tournament debutants Cape Verde on Wednesday, making the perfect start to their quest for a place at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup. The Black Queens, who suffered defeat in their opening match at the previous edition, ensured there would be no repeat this time as an early Doris Boaduwaa strike and a second-half own goal secured all three points in the Group D opener. Victory also preserved Ghana’s impressive record against WAFCON debutants, with the Black Queens once again proving too strong for newcomers on the continental stage. Ghana came into the match knowing that reaching the semi-finals would secure automatic qualification for the 2027 Women’s World Cup in Brazil, making a positive start essential. The breakthrough arrived after only six minutes. A superb pass from Portia Boakye released Doris Boaduwaa, who timed her run perfectly before calmly finishing to give Ghana a dream start. The early goal settled some early nerves after both teams had looked unsettled during the opening exchanges. Although Ghana enjoyed more possession, neither side found much rhythm in the early stages. Cape Verde struggled to make the right decisions in the final third, while the Queens were also guilty of misplacing passes and failing to consistently find their attacking players. The Black Queens nevertheless remained the more threatening side. Boaduwaa almost doubled her tally midway through the first half after another promising attacking move, while Ghana twice came close from corner kicks, only to see the chances narrowly evade the finishing touch. At the other end, Cape Verde threatened sporadically and forced Ghana into a few anxious moments defensively. However, goalkeeper Cynthia Konlan remained composed whenever called upon, helping her side maintain their slender advantage. Boaduwaa continued to cause problems throughout the opening period and came within inches of scoring her second after excellent work from Alice Kusi created another clear opportunity. Despite creating the better chances, Ghana went into the interval with only a one-goal lead. The scoreline did not fully reflect the Black Queens’ superiority, but they had controlled possession for long spells and restricted Cape Verde’s attacking opportunities. The second half followed a similar pattern, with Ghana searching for the goal that would effectively seal the contest. Chantelle Boye-Hlorkah delivered an inviting cross towards Boaduwaa, but before the forward could apply the finishing touch, Cape Verde defender Eleia Vieira inadvertently diverted the ball into her own net to double Ghana’s advantage. The victory sends Ghana temporarily to the top of Group D, pending the outcome of the later match between Mali and Cameroon. The Black Queens return to action on August 2, when they face Cameroon in their second group game.

items.title: HRCP, Amnesty call for 'prompt, independent' probe into Rawalakot unrest
items.description: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) and Amnesty International have expressed concern over reports of violence in the Rawalakot area of Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s (AJK) Poonch district, and called on the authorities to probe the incidents. Clashes took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Rawalakot on Monday and Mirpur on Tuesday, which reportedly resulted in several casualties. The now-proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now. The government has accused militant elements “pu­r­­s­u­ing a foreign age­nda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the unrest. The tensions come as elections are being held across AJK in three division-wise phases . In a statement published on Tuesday, the HRCP said it was “deeply alarmed” at reports of deaths and injuries in clashes between protesters and law enforcement personnel in AJK’s Rawalakot area on Monday. “The reported deaths in Rawalakot are a stark reminder of the human cost of the tensions that have gripped AJK in recent weeks,” the HRCP said. “While the authorities have a duty to maintain public order, this must never come at the expense of the right to life or the freedoms of peaceful assembly and expression,” it added. HRCP urged an end to the “cycle of violence” and called for a “prompt, impartial and independent investigation” into the reports of deaths and injuries. It also called for “anyone responsible for unlawful use of force to be held to account”. “We also urge the authorities to exercise restraint in responding to protests. As the remaining phases of the elections approach, the focus must shift from confrontation to protecting lives and restoring public confidence,” the statement concluded. Meanwhile, Amnesty International called on authorities to lift a communications blackout in the region. The statement , quoting Amnesty International’s Acting Regional Director for South Asia Isabelle Lassee, sought a “prompt, independent, and transparent investigation” into the reported use of force against protesters. “So long as an internet and mobile services blackout remains in place, it will severely impede the independent verification of the full extent of the situation on the ground. We urge the Pakistani authorities to restore all communications access and allow media and independent observers into the area,” she stated. Internet services restored in parts of Muzaffarabad On Wednesday, internet services were restored in parts of Muzaffarabad division after remaining suspended for 54 days, bringing relief to residents who had repeatedly demanded an end to the blanket shutdown imposed on the night of June 5. It was not immediately clear whether the restoration covered the entire Muzaffarabad division or was limited to the state capital. The unexpected restoration was greeted with relief by residents. However, many users complained that cellular data remained painfully slow, similar to the situation in Mirpur, and hoped the authorities would improve the service without further delay. Amid the suspension of mobile services in several parts of AJK, it has been difficult to obtain information from residents and officials in those areas. Secondary officials have also refrained from commenting on the situation. The authorities had restored internet services in Mirpur division on July 23, four days before polling in the first phase of the elections. Although the situation in Muzaffarabad and Mirpur divisions had largely returned to normal, the authorities had continued to withhold internet services in both divisions despite repeated appeals from residents, businesses, students and political leaders. Over the past month, the regional administration and the JAAC have been at odds over various issues, most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 seats in the region’s Legislative Assembly, which has resulted in protests across the region. On June 5, following the announcement of the JAAC’s June 9 strike, the AJK government declared the committee a proscribed organisation and placed it under the First Schedule of the region’s anti-terrorism act (ATA). The next day, AJK authorities launched a crackdown on the JAAC, arresting scores of its leaders and later placing 147 of its activists on the Fourth Schedule of the ATA. On Tuesday, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said that JAAC were not peaceful but violent, alleging the involvement of militant elements pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding. “Peaceful and transparent elections were held in AJK, with all the mainstream political parties participating fully. The people of Kashmir responded to the call of the election,” he stated, referring to the first phase of elections held in Mirpur division on Monday. However, he said, the banned outfit could not accept this political activity, nor the peaceful and transparent elections. Additional input by Tariq Naqash

items.title: Osun 2026: INEC has no preferred candidate, political allegiance – Amupitan
items.description: By Shina Abubakar The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Professor Joash Amupitan has assured stakeholders ahead of the August 15 governorship election in Osun State that the commission has no preferred candidate or political allegiance to anyone. He also urged residents in the State not to be deterred by the spread of violence, saying adequate security will be provided, tasking them to throng polling units en masse to cast their votes for their preferred candidates. Speaking at a stakeholders meeting including political parties, civil society organisation and others in Osogbo on Wednesday, he said the commission as an unbias umpire is neutral and would organize credible election in the state. “The Independent National Electoral Commission has no preferred candidate, holds no political allegiance, and seeks no outcome other than the lawful choice of the electorate, our sole loyalty is to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the sovereign will of the Nigerian people,” Amupitan mentioned. He added that democracy can only thrive when citizens exercise their constitutional right to vote, describing voter apathy as one of the greatest threats to Nigeria’s democratic progress. “Apathy is the silent killer of democratic progress, and we must confront it head-on.” He added that “the finest technology and the best-secured polling units mean little if they remain empty,” he said. Amupitan appealed directly to the people of Osun, urging them not to allow fear, apathy or misinformation to keep them away from the polls. “Do not allow fear, apathy, or misinformation to silence your voice. Turn out peacefully on Saturday, 15th August 2026, vote your conscience, and trust that this Commission will protect the sanctity of every valid ballot. “Our commitment is simple: no citizen should have to choose between their safety and their right to vote,” he mentioned. Amupitan further appealed to accredited journalists to report the election professionally and urged domestic and international observer groups to carry out their responsibilities objectively. He also reminded political parties and candidates to uphold the Peace Accord, warning that “rhetoric that incites violence or the deployment of political thugs will be met with decisive state force.” He called on all eligible voters to come out in mass on election day and make their voices heard through the ballot box, saying, “let the streets of Osun State lead to the polling units on that day. Let your voices be heard, and let your votes count”. The post Osun 2026: INEC has no preferred candidate, political allegiance – Amupitan appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Health Minister outlines measures for safe storage and distribution of medical products
items.description: The Minister for Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, has outlined a series of measures being implemented by the government to ensure the safe storage and distribution of pharmaceutical and other medical products across the country in line with international standards. He said the Food and Drugs Authority’s (FDA) guidelines are aligned with the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) recommendations and apply to all businesses involved in the storage and distribution of medical products. According to the Minister, the guidelines are intended to safeguard the safety, quality and efficacy of medicines and other health products throughout the supply chain. Mr Akandoh explained that, under the Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851), the FDA has established licensing guidelines for medical product storage facilities and continues to strengthen compliance through regular capacity-building programmes. He noted that pharmacists, supply chain managers, warehouse personnel and logistics officers have been receiving continuous training on the WHO’s Good Storage and Distribution Practices to enhance their knowledge and skills. The Health Minister made the disclosure on the floor of Parliament in response to a question from the Member of Parliament for Offinso North, Fred Kyei Asamoah. He assured the House that the measures being implemented would help build a resilient, transparent and efficient health supply chain capable of delivering quality-assured medical products to all levels of Ghana’s healthcare system.

items.title: Too young for sugar sickness: The rise of diabetes among children in Ghana
items.description: In today’s competitive job market, many parents have to wake up early to prepare their children for school while also getting ready for work. After school, these children often have to wait for their parents, who may return home late, making it a tiring cycle for the young ones. Unfortunately, the eating habits of these families, especially for children, raise significant concerns. Processed snacks, sugary drinks, sweetened milk, and “grab-and-go” foods have replaced traditional meals in many households. Items like biscuits, meat pies, boxed juice, and sugary cereals are now common, while healthier options like beans, kontomire, fish, and tubers are often overlooked. With parents working long hours, leaving home before dawn and returning late, cooking can feel impossible on busy mornings. This leads to lunch bags filled with packaged snacks instead of home-cooked meals. Additionally, in our digital age, children are spending more time in front of screens and engaging in less physical activity. Fewer children walk to school, play outside, or do household chores; they often stay indoors due to safety concerns, traffic, and the allure of screen time. The combination of less physical activity and poor eating habits contributes to weight gain, which increases the risk of diabetes. Unfortunately, by the time a blood test is conducted, blood sugar levels may be dangerously high. Untreated diabetes in childhood can lead to long-term complications affecting the eyes, kidneys, nerves and heart as well as negatively impacting school performance and mental health. This alarming trend should be a significant concern, particularly as Type 2 diabetes cases among children continue to surge. While Ghana does not currently have a national count of child diabetes cases, hospital and research data from the Ghana Health Service indicate an upward trend, especially for Type 2 diabetes among children. A study conducted in Kumasi by the Ghana Health Service involving 106 children and adolescents with newly diagnosed diabetes showed that 84.9% had Type 1 diabetes and 15.1% had Type 2. Notably, Type 2 cases were predominantly female, aged 9 to 19 years, and Type 1 cases peaked at ages 12 to 13. The Diabetes, Endocrine and Metabolic Society of Ghana has reported a rising number of Type 2 diabetes cases among children, yet diagnoses often come late, usually when severe complications occur. The broader issue here is that childhood diabetes is increasingly challenging because it is often unexpected. If your child experiences constant thirst, frequent urination, unexplained tiredness, or weight loss, it is essential to consult a clinic for a blood sugar test. Early detection significantly simplifies management. We must also reconsider our lifestyles and make adjustments. It is not necessary to send your children to a school close to your workplace if it is far away. Waking children up too early can lead to fatigue. This accumulated tiredness, combined with unhealthy eating habits such as increased consumption of processed snacks, sugary drinks, and sweetened milk, contributes to the rise in diabetes among children. Parents need to prioritise cooking healthy meals and regularly incorporating fruits and vegetables into their diets. Additionally, children should be encouraged to participate in outdoor activities instead of spending all their time on devices or in front of the television. The health of our children should be treated with urgency. Our children are not meant to carry the weight of our busy schedules in their lunch bags, or in their blood sugar levels. The rise of diabetes among Ghanaian children is not about bad parenting. It is about a fast-paced life, easy snacks and habits we adopted without realising the cost. Sources : Ghana Health Service, Diabetes, Endocrine Metabolism Society of Ghana.

items.title: Peace is an investment Ghana must continuously protect – Hannah Tetteh
items.description: United Nations Special Representative Hannah Tetteh has cautioned Ghana against taking its peace and security for granted, warning that instability in neighbouring countries demonstrates how quickly situations can change. She said Ghana’s stability must be treated as a continuous investment that requires deliberate effort and attention. Speaking at the 21st Kronti ne Akwamu Public Lecture, Mrs Tetteh said while Ghana has enjoyed relative peace, developments in other parts of the region show that such stability cannot be assumed. “We cannot take our peace and security for granted. And we should not assume that because we haven’t been hit by those kind of conflicts yet, it will not happen,” she said. She warned that conflicts often destroy infrastructure and development gains built over many years, leaving affected countries with the difficult task of rebuilding while carrying existing financial obligations. Mrs Tetteh said Ghana’s proximity to countries experiencing security challenges, particularly in the Sahel region, makes regional stability a national concern. She stressed the need for stronger cooperation within West Africa to manage emerging security risks. The UN envoy also linked peace and security to economic development, arguing that instability can reverse years of progress and discourage investment. She said the country’s economic recovery efforts must be supported by policies that reduce vulnerability to external shocks. Mrs Tetteh noted that Ghana’s foreign policy choices should complement efforts to build economic resilience and protect national interests. She encouraged Ghanaian leaders and citizens to view peacebuilding as an ongoing process. “Peace building even within a national context should be seen as an investment that we must be making on a continuous basis. It’s like a garden. You need to tend to it,” she said. Mrs Tetteh said maintaining peace requires inclusive governance, strong institutions and sustained attention to potential sources of instability. She added that Ghana’s experience should serve as a reminder that peace is valuable and must be actively protected.

items.title: ‘It’s a golden opportunity’ – Infantino defends FIFA World Cup commercial proposal
items.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino said Wednesday that the proposed launch of a private subsidiary to expoit the commercial benefits of the World Cup was “an opportunity but not an obligation”. A proposal to sell stakes in FIFA’s major competitions sparked disbelief and outrage globally since it was revealed Tuesday, but Infantino defended the idea, saying too little of football’s commercial value reached the parts of the game that need it most. “FIFA Forward Enterprise, or FFE, is actually a proposal, an offer. It’s part of a democratic process – a consultation process – and, above all, it is an opportunity but not an obligation,” Infantino said in a video released Wednesday evening. “It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally. But again, it is just an offer, not an obligation.” Infantino insisted the proposal was centred on unlocking “previously uncaptured commercial value” and was conditional on a democratic vote of FIFA’s 211 member associations and approval by the FIFA council. “Capturing that value requires additional expertise, additional insight, distinct from governing and developing the sport,” he said. “It would simply commercialise and organise all FIFA-owned competitions along with sponsorship, broadcast, licensing and new ventures for the benefit of FIFA’s 211 member associations.” Infantino said the game would not change and the fans would be happier. “Fans from everywhere in the world would gain immeasurably from this game-changing potential because it will transform football in their countries,” he said. items.title: Omar Seghrouchni rejette le "faux débat" entre protection des données et droit à l'information
items.description: Le président de la Commission nationale de contrôle de la protection des données à caractère personnel (CNDP), Omar Seghrouchni, estime que les lois encadrant ces deux droits sont complémentaires et non concurrentes. Il appelle ainsi à dépasser ce qu'il qualifie de « faux débat » entre protection des données personnelles et droit d'accès à l'information. Dans une analyse, Seghrouchni, également à la tête de la Commission du droit d'accès à l'information (CDAI), rappelle que la loi 09.08, relative à la protection des données à caractère personnel, met en œuvre les dispositions de l'article 24 de la Constitution de 2011, consacré au respect de la vie privée. La loi 31.13, quant à elle, donne effet à l'article 27 garantissant le droit d'accès à l'information. Selon lui, l'enjeu n'est pas de privilégier l'un de ces droits au détriment de l'autre, mais d'assurer leur complémentarité afin de consolider l'État de droit. Le responsable souligne que la loi sur la protection des données personnelles ne se limite pas à encadrer le traitement des informations. Elle traduit également une conception fondée sur le respect de la dignité humaine, de la vie privée et des libertés individuelles, inspirée à la fois des principes universels et des traditions marocaines. Les organismes amenés à traiter des données personnelles sont ainsi tenus de respecter plusieurs obligations. Ils doivent notamment définir clairement la finalité de la collecte, limiter les données aux besoins strictement nécessaires, garantir leur sécurité, respecter les règles de conservation prévues par la loi et permettre aux personnes concernées d'exercer leurs droits d'accès, de rectification et, lorsque les conditions sont réunies, d'effacement. Évoquant le développement de l'intelligence artificielle et des systèmes de décision automatisés, Omar Seghrouchni insiste sur la nécessité de veiller à ce que ces technologies restent transparentes, compréhensibles et susceptibles d'être contrôlées. À ses yeux, ces garanties sont indispensables pour prévenir les décisions arbitraires et préserver la confiance des citoyens dans les usages numériques. Le président de la CNDP rappelle également que l'institution est chargée de contrôler les traitements de données personnelles dans les secteurs public et privé, tout en rendant des avis sur les projets de textes législatifs ou réglementaires lorsque le gouvernement ou le Parlement la saisissent. S'il reconnaît que le gouvernement n'est pas légalement tenu de consulter systématiquement la CNDP, Omar Seghrouchni estime qu'une telle pratique est difficilement conciliable avec les principes de bonne gouvernance. Il invite également le Parlement à inscrire explicitement dans son règlement intérieur un mécanisme de consultation de la Commission afin de garantir une meilleure application des dispositions légales. Concernant la loi 31.13, Seghrouchni rappelle qu'elle garantit aux citoyens le droit d'accéder aux informations détenues par les administrations publiques, les institutions élues et les organismes chargés d'une mission de service public, tout en prévoyant des exceptions destinées à protéger notamment la sécurité de l'État, les libertés fondamentales et la vie privée. Pour le président de la CDAI, le droit d'accès à l'information constitue un levier essentiel pour renforcer la transparence de l'action publique, le principe de reddition des comptes et le contrôle citoyen. Il y voit également un outil de lutte contre la désinformation et les fausses informations, estimant qu'une démocratie ne peut pleinement fonctionner sans un accès effectif à l'information. Il rappelle enfin que les missions de la CNDP et de la CDAI sont étroitement liées. Les deux institutions poursuivent, selon lui, un objectif commun : concilier la protection de la vie privée et le droit d'accès à l'information afin de renforcer la confiance des citoyens et de consolider l'État de droit. Pour conclure, Omar Seghrouchni appelle à dépasser toute lecture opposant ces deux droits. La protection des données personnelles et le droit d'accès à l'information constituent, selon lui, deux piliers d'une même culture démocratique, dont la mise en œuvre coordonnée est indispensable à une gouvernance plus transparente, plus responsable et respectueuse des droits et libertés fondamentaux. The post Omar Seghrouchni rejette le "faux débat" entre protection des données et droit à l'information appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
